_readme: SC id reservations. Read by lib/sc-reservations.ts and enforced by lib/create-sc.ts.
Declare your block HERE, on main, before you consume any id — including a renumber
during a repair, a hand-written fixture id, or a block chosen by eyeballing headroom.
A renumber is an allocation. See .claude/rules/parallel-sessions.md and issue #725.
Shape: every entry needs owner (branch name or issue ref), from and to (inclusive,
positive integers; below the 9000 fixture floor for SC). note is optional. Blocks
must not overlap — the reader refuses the whole store if two do, because a store
that hands one id to two owners is worse than no store at all.
namespace is optional and ABSENT MEANS SC, so every entry written before #1363
keeps its exact meaning. The store also holds FG (test/issue-filing-gate.test.ts)
and AR (test/finding-arbiter.test.ts), which have no allocator and so collide the
same way SC ids do. An unknown namespace refuses the whole store by name, and
overlap is judged WITHIN a namespace — FG 45-60 and SC 45-60 claim nothing in
common. Adding a namespace means editing RESERVATION_NAMESPACES in
lib/sc-reservations.ts and the table in .claude/rules/parallel-sessions.md.
The `reservations` key is the control string: an object without it is UNREADABLE,
not empty, and the allocator refuses rather than returning a number. Delete your
entry when your branch merges; a block nobody prunes is headroom nobody can use.
AN EMPTY LIST IS THE RESTING STATE, not a store nobody has filled in. It means no
branch is holding ids right now, and ids already written in specs/ are protected
by lib/create-sc.ts's `taken` set rather than by a block. Until #1969 two tests
required this list to be non-empty, so the last deletion was always red.
Before deleting somebody else's entry, check that its branch merged — one
`gh pr list --head <owner> --state all --json number,state` per entry. #1969
records that reading for the thirteen it cleared, PR by PR; this file cannot
prove it about itself, so do not read the sentence above as proof.
